title: Computed tomography (CT)-based gastric volumetry as a predictive factor for respiratory complications in polytrauma patients
summary:
Aspiration of gastric contents during endotracheal intubation is a risk factor for pulmonary complications. While the risk of aspiration is low during elective general anesthesia, it increases with unplanned airway management and is described with an incidence of <0.1% to 19% (J Clin Anesth 1998; 10: 95-102; Anesth Analg 2001; 93: 494-513; Crit Care Med 2003; 31: 1930-7; Anesth Analg 2006; 103: 941-7; Can J Anaesth 2007; 54: 748-64). A "safe" gastric volume, as a threshold for aspiration, does not yet exist. In addition, gastric emptying may be delayed due to stress such as trauma, pain or medication such as opioid analgesia, so that even after fasting there may be more gastric contents than in elective patients.
Therefore, in clinical practice, the presence of gastric contents (and volume) is the most important factor for aspiration prevention. Although the minimum volume of gastric contents that increases aspiration risk is not currently known, it is generally accepted that the baseline volume of gastric secretion in healthy fasting patients is safe and represents a very low risk in the order of 1:4000 anaesthetics (Cook TM, Woodall N, Frerk C. On behalf of the Royal College of Anaesthetists. Report and findings of the 4th National Audit Project of the Royal College of Anaesthetists. 2011; ISBN 978-1-90009 36-03-3). 
The hypothesis of the retrospective clinical study is that polytraumatized patients with a gastric volume of 2 ml/kg develop significantly more respiratory complications than patients with a gastric volume <1.5 ml/kg. The primary objective of the study is to use CT-based gastric volumetry to predict the risk of respiratory complications in polytraumatized patients. The primary endpoint of the clinical study is respiratory complications, summarized as composite outcome.

interventions.name: Determining a cut-off value of gastric volumes for identifying a “high-risk group” for the incidence of respiratory complications in polytraumatized patients

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age >18 years
- documented Injury severity score (ISS) >=16
- endotracheally intubated on admission to the university emergency center
- Inpatient stay >14 days
- Polytrauma CT immediately after admission to the trauma room and subsequent intensive care treatment
Exclusion criteria:
- Age <18 years
- documented injury severity score (ISS) <16
- length of inpatient stay <14 days
- no polytrauma CT on admission
- gastric tube in place on admission
- no intensive medical treatment
